answer: Policies are written in pulse, settled in vine, and bridge lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 30% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 100 aliases cost 185 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
